summary: A Norwegian municipality's report proposing school and kindergarten closures reportedly cited sources that do not exist, including a book falsely attributed to a professor. Officials admitted using AI to help write it, and the consultation on the plan was halted.
technical_summary: Municipal staff used a generative language model to help draft a 120-page policy report. The model fabricated references, and the draft was published without verifying citations, so only seven of 18 references could be traced.

technology.quote: admitted the report was written with AI

failure_mode.quote: Of 18 references in the report, only seven actually exist.

harm_type.quote: Of 18 references in the report, only seven actually exist.

affected_population.quote: The shutdown plan upset local residents.

notes: Officials say people wrote the report and AI was only a helper; excerpts are partly in Norwegian.

summary: Images of eight Iranian women political prisoners, reportedly AI-enhanced, were amplified by US officials with an unverified claim of imminent execution. Iran dismissed the claim as fake news, and analysts said the episode blurred real documentation with synthetic images.
technical_summary: AI tools were used to enhance real photographs so they looked synthetic, while fully AI-generated images circulated alongside them. Political accounts spread the collage with an unverified execution claim, making authentic evidence easier to dismiss.
systems: AI image enhancement and generation tools

technology.quote: AI tools are being used to enhance real photographs until they look manufactured

harm_type.quote: the credibility of the documentation that human rights work depends on is being eroded by people who claim to be defending them

affected_population.quote: Real Iranian women protesters are being held in Iranian prisons under threat of capital punishment.

notes: Reports differ on who enhanced the images; the execution claim was unverified and disputed by Iran.

summary: The FBI arrested a Wisconsin man accused of using Stable Diffusion to generate thousands of sexually explicit images of minors and sending some to a 15-year-old boy. It was among the first federal cases over fully AI-generated child sexual abuse material.
technical_summary: A text-to-image diffusion model was prompted with explicit text to create realistic images of minors, which were then shared via messaging and social platforms. Detection came through platform reports to the child-safety clearinghouse, not through safeguards in the model.

technology.quote: used a text-to-image generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) model called Stable Diffusion to create thousands of realistic images of prepubescent minors

failure_mode.quote: used a text-to-image generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) model called Stable Diffusion to create thousands of realistic images of prepubescent minors

harm_type.quote: sent him several of the AI generated images of minors through Instagram direct messages
CSAM generated by AI is still CSAM, and we will hold accountable those who exploit AI

affected_population.quote: sent him several of the AI generated images of minors through Instagram direct messages

notes: Allegations from charging documents; reports say the images did not depict real children.

summary: A purported AI-generated deepfake video showed a New Zealand diabetes expert and a TV journalist promoting a fake cure and telling viewers to stop their medication. People were reportedly deceived into buying products, and new versions kept appearing.
technical_summary: Synthetic video and audio impersonating a trusted clinician and broadcaster, with imperfect lip sync, were used in social media scam ads. The content steered patients away from prescribed treatment toward fraudulent products, and takedowns were quickly evaded by reposted variants.

technology.quote: The tell-tale signs videos had altered included a lack of synchronisation between the words being spoken and her mouth moving.

failure_mode.quote: conning Kiwis into dropping their medication and purchasing fake products

harm_type.quote: conning Kiwis into dropping their medication and purchasing fake products
The video was also convincing those with diabetes to stop taking important medications

affected_population.quote: The video was also convincing those with diabetes to stop taking important medications

severity.quote: The video was also convincing those with diabetes to stop taking important medications, prompting a warning from Health NZ

notes: Scale of victims unclear; police said they were not aware of victims who paid.

summary: Sheriff's deputies in Louisiana arrested a woman who had first been treated as a victim, saying she created fake accounts, AI-generated nude images and rape threats used in an extortion and impersonation campaign. Sexual images of one victim were sent to family and friends.
technical_summary: Generative image and video tools were used to produce fabricated nude media of a person, which was distributed to the victim's contacts alongside threats and payment demands made via fake accounts. Platform records and subpoenas traced the activity to the account holder.
systems: AI image and video generation tools

technology.quote: AI-generated photos and videos of one of the victims were also sent to numerous family members and friends

failure_mode.quote: AI-generated photos and videos of one of the victims were also sent to numerous family members and friends

one person was being threatened with rape and other bodily harm unless they paid money

notes: Allegations from the sheriff's office; charges are pending and the suspect is not named here.

summary: A high school in Pennsylvania and local police investigated an AI-generated video that depicted several students inappropriately. A juvenile was later charged with harassment, and parents called for better school policies and faster responses.
technical_summary: A student used a generative tool to create fake sexualized media of classmates and shared it. Consumer apps that can turn an ordinary photo into explicit content are widely available, and school policies did not clearly cover off-campus AI misuse.

summary: Reports described men in New York City's gay nightlife being drugged and robbed, with attackers reportedly using the victims' phone facial recognition to access banking apps and drain accounts. At least two men reportedly died.
technical_summary: Perpetrators used incapacitated victims' faces to unlock phones secured by facial recognition, then moved money through payment and banking apps. The attack exploits biometric authentication that works on an unconscious person.

technology.quote: robbed using their phone's facial recognition tech, and killed

failure_mode.quote: robbed using their phone's facial recognition tech, and killed

severity.quote: At least 2 men were drugged, robbed using their phone's facial recognition tech, and killed

notes: Police had not said whether the deaths and the account thefts were linked or whether victims were targeted for being gay.

summary: After Meta released its LLaMA language model as open source, people reportedly used it to build graphic sexual chatbots, some of which role-play violent scenes such as rape. The report raised questions about open-source release and responsibility.
technical_summary: An openly released large language model was fine-tuned or prompted by individual developers into explicit role-play chatbots without the guardrails of hosted services, enabling violent and illegal sexual content with little oversight.

technology.quote: people are already using Meta's large language model (LLM), LLaMA

failure_mode.quote: can reportedly include violent scenes of rape and abuse fantasies

notes: Concern is largely potential harm; the excerpt reports no specific victim of the explicit chatbots.

summary: Scammers reportedly used fake TikTok accounts impersonating Spain's Princess Leonor, some with AI-mimicked voice and likeness, to promise cash prizes and then demand escalating fees. Victims in Latin America lost money.
technical_summary: Dozens of fake social media profiles used AI-generated voice and imagery of a royal to build trust, while the platform's engagement algorithm amplified them. Victims were drawn into advance-fee fraud with repeated payment demands.

technology.quote: used artificial intelligence to mimic Leonor's voice and likeness

notes: Only some fake accounts are reported to use AI; the scheme itself is a conventional advance-fee fraud.

summary: A fictional story about a Boy Scout who vanished in 1989 and reappeared in 2001 spread across YouTube, TikTok and blogs as if true. Fact-checkers found it was made with AI-generated narration, images and footage, and the case never existed.
technical_summary: A YouTube channel produced fictional missing-person videos using AI-generated voice and imagery, which were then cut into short clips and rewritten into AI-written blog posts. Platform recommendation systems pushed the content to millions as real.

technology.quote: whose owner shares fictional stories in lengthy videos generated with the help of artificial intelligence

harm_type.quote: AI was making them easier to mass-produce and more believable to unsuspecting viewers

notes: The named boy is fictional. Creator intent (entertainment or engagement bait) is unclear.

summary: A Coco delivery robot reportedly crashed into a glass bus shelter in Chicago, shattering panels across the sidewalk. The company said nobody was hurt, called it rare and isolated, and accepted responsibility for repair costs while investigating.
technical_summary: A self-driving sidewalk delivery robot operating under a city pilot collided with a glass structure. Neither operator explained what caused the robot to drive into the shelter. A similar crash by a competitor's robot had occurred days earlier.

harm_type.quote: a self-driving food delivery robot has crashed into a CTA bus shelter, sending shards of glass all over the sidewalk

severity.quote: Video and photos show glass strewn across the sidewalk and on top of the robot.

notes: Cause not yet explained by the company; failure mode inferred.

summary: Anthropic reported that criminals misused its Claude models, including a data-extortion campaign against at least 17 organizations using Claude Code, North Korean fraudulent job schemes, and sales of AI-generated ransomware. The company banned the accounts and added safeguards.
technical_summary: An agentic coding tool was used to automate reconnaissance, credential theft, intrusion, data analysis, ransom-setting and extortion messaging against organizations. Other actors used the model to build ransomware and fake identities, showing AI lowering barriers to sophisticated cybercrime despite safeguards.

sector.quote: targeted at least 17 distinct organizations, including in healthcare, the emergency services, and government and religious institutions
